## Catalog requirements

With the aid of an academic advisor, the BSIS student devises a course plan to meet the graduation requirements: ten core courses, five major electives, professional writing, and four open electives, for a total of twenty courses (60 credits). At least 45 of the 60 credits must be courses taken from the College of Information.
The Bachelor of Science degree will be awarded to the student who successfully completes a program of 120 undergraduate hours, with a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale for all courses taken for undergraduate credit since matriculation into the program. A student whose cumulative grade point average at any time in the program is lower than 2.0 is automatically placed on academic probation by the College until the problem leading to probationary status has been corrected. Students have one semester to raise their GPA over 2.0.
Upon completion of all degree requirements, students will earn a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree from the College of Information at the University of Maryland College Park.

All BSIS at Shady Grove students need to have successfully completed (with a C- or better) all benchmark courses or their equivalents prior to taking program courses.

## Department page (https://ischool.umd.edu/academics/bachelors-programs/bachelor-of-science-in-information-science-shady-grove)

Bachelor of Science in Information Science at Shady Grove (InfoSci)
Apply now for Fall 2027! For best consideration, apply by March 1, 2027. The final deadline for submitting applications is June 1, 2027. To learn more, connect now (external link, opens in a new tab) with the program team.
The Bachelor of Science in Information Science (InfoSci) degree program at The Universities at Shady Grove [External Link] campus in Montgomery County is designed for transfer students who have completed their associate’s degree or equivalent. The InfoSci Shady Grove program teaches students skills in technical areas such as database design, information architecture, web/mobile development, data analytics, and cybersecurity alongside areas of the social sciences, leadership, and the humanities – addressing the growing and unique need for information professionals who understand complex social and organizational issues.
This innovative curriculum blends theory, practical skills, and hands-on learning, preparing our graduates to apply their skills directly and immediately in their careers. Our students work on projects with the UMD INFO College’s 400+ top industry partners and have opportunities for hands-on learning at the college’s world-renowned research centers and labs.
InfoSci graduates go on to careers in data science and analytics, database administration, UX/UI, technology development, digital curation, cybersecurity, web content and development, systems architecture, and more.

The Bachelor of Science in Information Science (InfoSci) at The Universities at Shady Grove is for transfer students with 60 credits or an Associate’s degree in a related field. Students complete the program in four semesters, taking five 3-credit courses per semester, with a pre-set schedule to ensure timely graduation.
Benchmark Courses set students up for success in the program and create foundational knowledge. Courses include Precalculus, Introduction to Psychology, Elementary Statistics and Probability, and more.
Program Courses allow students to become experts in the field, with courses like Information Organization, Database Design and Modeling, Dynamic Web Applications, and Advanced Data Science.
Visit the InfoSci at Shady Grove curriculum page for more details.
The INFO College also offers three academic minors to UMD undergraduate students. InfoDesign students can choose from these minors or others offered at UMD.
The Technology Innovation Leadership Minor
The Information Risk Management, Ethics, and Privacy Minor, Science, Technology
Ethics and Policy (STEP) Minor

More Info for Prospective Students
A bachelor’s degree in Information Science from the top-ranked UMD College of Information will equip you with the skills and credentials needed to launch a successful career as an information professional across all types of organizations – including government institutions, non-profits, educational and cultural institutions, the private sector, and the intelligence community.
INFO graduates have gone on to work at leading organizations like IBM, Google, the Library of Congress, National Archives, the Smithsonian, the CIA, IMF, Discovery Channel, the National Agricultural Library, the New York Times, and National Geographic, among others.
To help you prepare for and kickstart your career, the UMD College of Information offers a variety of resources for both students and alumni. Check out the Career Resources and the Careers Paths pages to learn more.
INFO’s faculty, staff, and 2800+ students come from over 61 countries and create a welcoming and encouraging environment. 56% of students identify as male, 45% female, 1% other; 63% of students identify Asian (29%), Black (24%), White (22%), Hispanic/Latino (9%), Biracial (4%), American Indian or Alaskan Native (<1%), Pacific Islander (<1%), Unknown/Other (12%). The INFO College is committed to bringing together many perspectives to foster deeper understanding and innovation.
At UMD students can also choose from hundreds of student organizations [External Link], including INFO student organizations, service opportunities, and social activities.

Tuition
In-State (Maryland resident) tuition is $5,904.50 per semester for full-time undergraduate students.
Out-of-State (Non-Resident) tuition is $20,593.00 per semester for Non-Resident full-time undergraduate students.
The Mandatory fees are a flat rate of $397.00 for 1-8 credit hours and $861.00 for 9+ credit hours.
View the detailed breakdown of undergraduate tuition & fees [External Link].
Financial Aid
The UMD INFO College provides financial aid to select current students who demonstrate academic excellence. Students may also reduce their tuition costs by serving as a TA or GA at UMD, but please note that these positions are competitive. There are also additional sources of financial aid offered by the University and by outside sources.
Learn more about financial aid here and check out the UMD Scholarship Management Tool [External Link].

USG prepares students for careers in high-demand fields—offering academic coaching, career advising, and internship placement. Graduates earn degrees from partner universities, backed by a shared commitment to their success.
Get to know USG and enjoy an active, close-knit community with small class sizes, academic support, and real-world experiences. Together, we make it happen.
